page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, 8 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, indicating a limitation for single-threaded execution. However, multi-core performance under stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests ranks in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show average performance, though the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also weak, while database operations and Redis SET operations maintain average throughput.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this server presents a tradeoff between resource density and guaranteed compute performance. It is suited for workloads that can leverage multi-threaded execution without requiring sustained peak single-core performance, such as software compilation, text processing, and light database operations. It is less suitable for intensive single-threaded tasks, high-throughput web serving, or medium-to-large language model inference, where text generation speeds fall into the bottom 10%.
